 Hon'Ble Siddharth, J.

-
Heard Sri Dhirendra Singh Rajput, learned counsel for revisionist; Sri Dhirendra Bahadur Singh,
learned counsel for opposite party no. 4; learned A.G.A for State and perused the material on record.
-
The present criminal revision has been filed against the impugned order dated 19.03.2025 passed by Learned Additional District & Session Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act) Jalaun at Orai in Criminal Appeal No. 08 of 2025, Raghuvir vs. State of U.P., and against the order of dated 24.01.2025 passed by Juvenile Justice Board, Jalaun at Orai in Case No. 03/2017 (State vs. X S/o Y) arising out Case Crime No. 99/2017, under Section 376, 452 I.P.C. and Section POCSO Act Police Station- Kotwali Jalaun, District- Jalaun.

- 
As per the prosecution case, an application was submitted by the father of the victim on 01.12.2017,
wherein it was alleged that on 01.07.2017, at about 7:00 p.m., he along with his wife had gone to the field, leaving behind his elder daughter, aged about 14 years, at home.
During their absence, the accused-revisionist, a resident of the same locality, entered their house and, after throwing the victim on the cot, attempted to disrobe her.

On her raising of alarm, her younger sister, Jayawanti,
reached the place of incident, upon which the accused fled away.
On returning home, the father was apprised of the incident by his daughters, whereafter he filed the aforesaid application.
The matter was registered as Case Crime No. 99 of 2017, under Sections 376/511 and 452 of the I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of the POCSO Act.
After investigation, a charge-sheet was submitted against the accused under Sections 376 and 452 of the I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of the POCSO Act.
The accused was subsequently declared juvenile by the Juvenile Justice Board vide order dated 18.03.2017.

sentences.text: The statement of the revisionist was recorded under Section 251 Cr.P.C to disprove the prosecution case.

-
P.W.-1 in his statement before the court alleged that the revisionist after entering her house threw the victim on cot and committed the offence of rape against her and disrobbed her.

However in his cross-examination he admitted that when the accused threw his daughter on the cot and started disrobing her she raised alarm and his younger daughter, P.W.-2, came and thereafter accused-revisionist ran away.
He stated that this was the recital in the F.I.R which was correct.
P.W.-5 made clear allegation of commission of rape against P.W.-4 by the revisionist.

-
P.W.-3, the mother of the victim, stated in her statement that after throwing the victim on the cot and disrobing her, the revisionist continued to commit the alleged offence.
When her younger daughter, Jayanti, came on hearing the cries of the victim, the accused ran away.
In her cross-examination, P.W.-3 admitted that when she reached the house, she observed that the clothes of P.W.-4 were torn and that there was blood oozing from various parts of her body.
She further stated that neither police took the clothes nor did she gave it to the police.
The victim has gone to the police station in torn clothes.
She has suffered abrasions on her entire back and chest.
She admitted that she has not seen the incident but denied that she has any enmity with family of accused.

-
P.W.-4, stated in her statement that the accused entered into her house beated and disrobed her and committed the offence of rape against her.
When she raised alarm her sister, P.W.-2, came and she was also beaten by the accused.
She had gave the same statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C before the Magistrate.
She further stated that she had sustained injuries on her head, and that bleeding had came from wounds on her cheeks, back, hands, and private part.
Her father has given correct version of the incident in the F.I.R., stating that blood had fallen at the place of incident but the police did not collect any sample thereof.

-
P.W.-5 proved the lodging of F.I.R and entry of the same in the general diary of police station.

-
P.W.-6 proved that the mother of the victim had refused to get her internal examination.
She conducted only her external examination and observed a small old injury on the left cheek and injuries on her back in the form of a haematoma.

She opined that the injuries were caused to the Juvenile X vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111682769/
3 victim by hand and blunt object.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She admitted that the injury on cheek could have been caused by slapping and injury on back could have been caused by use of force against the victim on the cot.

-
P.W.-7, the Investigating Officer, proved the investigation conducted by him.
In his cross-examination, he admitted that he recorded the statement of the victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C., after a period of 50?54 days from the date of the incident.
He further admitted that no blood was found at the place of incident.
He also stated that the victim neither handed over her blood-stained clothes nor did he seized the same.
He further stated that during the statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim never informed him about the commission of the offence of rape against her.
He further stated that the victim stated that the incident had taken place on the terrace of the house, which is about 10?12 feet high, but there were no stairs leading to the terrace.

-
Learned counsel for the revisionist has submitted that the F.I.R was lodged on 02.02.2017 when the incident took place on 01.12.2013.
In the statement of victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C there is no allegation of commission of offence of rape and nor it is there in the statements of P.W.-2 and P.W.-3.
The statement of victim was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C after more than 164 days of the incident and was not reliable.
There was no explanation why the internal examination of the victim was refused at the time of medical examination of revisionist.
Revisionist was aged about 13 years, 09 months and 26 days only when the age of victim was about 14 years.
The revisionist has undergone sentence of about nine and a half months in all.
The conviction and sentence of revisionist is not in accordance with the material on record or the law.

The Juvenile Justice Board convicted the revisionist and sentenced him to undergo three years' imprisonment under Section 376 IPC, two years' imprisonment under Section 452 IPC, and two years' imprisonment under Section 4 of the POCSO Act, directing that all the sentences shall run concurrently.

-
The Appellate Court has confirmed the judgment of the Juvenile Justice Board and hence this revision.

-
After hearing the rival submissions, this court finds that from the statements of P.W.-1, P.W.-3,
P.W.-6 and P.W.-7, that commission of offence of rape does not appears to be proved.

Although there is no contradiction in the statement of victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C and her statement before the court but the fact remains that her statement was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C after more than 50 days by the Investigating Officer before Magistrate.
Therefore the possibility of tutoring P.W.-4, the victim, cannot be ruled out.

In the case, the offence of rape was committed by the revisionist against P.W.-4 why her internal medical examination was refused Juvenile X vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111682769/
4 before the Doctor was not explained by the prosecution.

sentences.text:
-
No clothes of the victim were recovered by P.W.-7, nor were they handed over to the police by P.W.-3 or P.W.-4 to establish the commission of the alleged offence.
From the F.I.R., read in conjunction with the cross-examination of P.W.-1, it appears that, at most, the offence of disrobing the victim by the revisionist by use of criminal force is made out.
Therefore, he ought to have been tried as an accused committing a serious offence under Section 354-B IPC, in accordance with Section 14(5)(e) of the Act.
However, he has been punished for the commission of offences under Sections 376/452 IPC and Section 4 of the POCSO Act.
The offence under Section 4 of the POCSO Act is not established.
Since the offence of penetrative sexual assault has not been proved against the victim, the conviction under Section 4 of the POCSO Act is not justified.
At most, the revisionist may have committed an offence under Sections 7/8 of the POCSO Act.
Consequently, the conviction of the revisionist under Sections 376/452 IPC and Section 4 of the POCSO Act cannot be sustained.
The remand of the matter for re-trial under the provisions of Section 14(5)(e) of the Juvenile Justice Act would not be in the interest of justice.
It is admitted that the revisionist was less than 14 years of age at the time of the incident.
He has already undergone custody for a period of approximately nine and a half months.
Accordingly, his conviction and sentence are converted to sentences under Sections 354-B, 452 IPC, and Sections 7/8 of the POCSO Act.

The revisionist shall undergo punishment of one year each under all the converted sections which shall run concurrently, and the period already served in custody shall be adjusted against the total period of sentence.

-
The criminal revision is partly allowed.

-
Let the record be returned to the trial court within one week.

-
The revisionist shall be released from custody after completing the total period of sentence of one year.

-
This order shall be communicated to the Juvenile Justice Board by the Registrar (Compliance)
within one week.

(Siddharth,J.) September 8, 2025 Rohit  Juvenile X vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111682769/
